prior_works.title: ARK
prior_works.relationship_sentence: Provides the ARK-style retrieval architecture (two graph tools with a controller that balances global lexical search and one-hop neighborhood exploration) that the current paper uses as the exact unconditioned baseline whose controller behavior is isolated from dataset and metric changes.

prior_works.title: STARK
prior_works.relationship_sentence: Introduced the text-rich knowledge-graph benchmark suite (PRIME, MAG, Amazon) and evaluation protocols that the paper holds fixed while testing profile/trace interventions, supplying the concrete graphs and metrics against which retrieval quality is measured.

prior_works.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting
prior_works.relationship_sentence: Established the paradigm of emitting reasoning traces interleaved with environment actions, directly inspiring the paper's design of trace-conditioned hints and the idea of exposing intermediate observations to a retrieval controller.

prior_works.title: Reflexion
prior_works.relationship_sentence: Showed iterative self-improvement via reflective feedback but also exposed that feedback loops can fail without appropriate action policies, motivating the current investigation into when observation-level feedback can harm rather than help retrieval.

prior_works.title: Think-on-Graph
prior_works.relationship_sentence: Demonstrated methods for exposing graph traversal and neighborhood reasoning to language models, providing the concrete graph-tool action primitives (traverse, inspect node text, follow relations) that the paper's controller protocol exercises and diagnoses.

prior_works.title: Personalize Before Retrieve (PBR)
prior_works.relationship_sentence: Argued that compact pre-retrieval user state should shape retrieval actions, directly motivating the paper's 'profile' conditioning probe and the question whether pre-retrieval signals can be injected as prompt context without a calibrated action policy.

prior_works.title: AgentBench
prior_works.relationship_sentence: Advocated instrumentation-first agent evaluation with trajectory-level measurements, inspiring the paper's paired trajectory counters and the decision to attribute failures to observable trajectory behaviors rather than only to final scores.

synthesis_narrative: 近期若干研究共同提供了本文所使用的技术构件与实证视角。ARK 系列给出了具体的控制器-工具架构（控制器在全局词法搜索与一跳邻域探索之间进行权衡），而 "STARK" 基准贡献了文本丰富图集合（PRIME、MAG、Amazon）以及本研究刻意保持固定的标准排序指标。关于交错进行推理与行动的智能体研究，尤其是 "ReAct"，为输出轨迹并将中间观察作为控制器输入提供了动机，而 "Reflexion" 则同时凸显了迭代反馈的潜力与边界条件——表明观察反馈只有在实质改变动作选择时才有帮助。"Think-on-Graph" 为 LM 驱动的探索提供了具体的图遍历原语与遍历语义，"Personalize Before Retrieve (PBR)" 则提出了紧凑的检索前状态应影响检索决策这一思想。最后，"AgentBench" 提供了以 instrumentation 为先的评估理念与轨迹计数器，为过程级归因奠定基础。总体而言，这些工作揭示了一个自然但尚未充分探索的缺口：加入检索前画像或观察轨迹会改变控制器的动作分布，因此除非重新校准动作策略，否则可能损害排序输出。该缺口促成了本文的轻量级画像/轨迹诊断协议：在固定的 "STARK" 图上叠加 ARK 风格控制器，输出紧凑的检索前画像与简短轨迹提示，记录配对轨迹计数器，并使用共享 ID 配对差值来定位失败（重复调用、零结果调用、预算错配）——从而将“检索前思考”视为对动作的控制问题，而不仅仅是提示格式的变化。
